top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a verified, independently reproduced achievement with a clean allocation: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice concept and first strontium lattice clock, and Ye's development of the many-atom clock to the 10^-18 level with resolved many-body physics. Several laboratories have reproduced and surpassed the results, and the lattice-shift and blackbody corrections are quantitatively understood theory tied to measurement. I rank a new state of matter above a measurement capability, but no defensible condensed-matter slate is available, and awarding this mature, well-credited work is better than no award.
